title: Simply GitLab configuration baseline
description: What a set of GitLab projects should have in common. Read by `simply gitlab config plan` and `simply gitlab config apply`. Advisory: the CLI's own validator is what runs, and its errors name the exact path that is wrong.

overrides.description: Per-target exceptions, keyed by full project or group path.

targets.description: What the run acts on. Groups expand through their subgroups.

groups.description: Group paths or ids. Each expands to every project in the group and its subgroups.

projects.description: Individual project paths or ids, added to whatever the groups expanded to.

exclude.description: Removed from the union. A trailing * drops a whole subtree.

settings.description: Attributes for PUT /groups/:id. Names are GitLab's own.
Attributes for PUT /projects/:id — merge method, CI config path, build timeout, and the rest. Names are GitLab's own; only what you declare is compared.

protectedBranches.description: Branch protections, keyed by name. Corrected in place with PATCH.

protectedTags.description: Tag protections, keyed by name. GitLab has no update endpoint, so a change is a delete and a create.

approvalRules.description: Approval rules, keyed by name (Premium/Ultimate). Accepts `usernames`, group paths under `groups`, and branch names under `protectedBranches`; the ids are resolved for you.

variables.description: CI/CD variable metadata, keyed by key + environment_scope. Reported only, never written: creating or updating a variable requires its value, and this file holds none.

section.description: A list section: a bare array, or an object that can also prune or replace.

prune.description: Delete entries that exist on the instance but are not declared here. Off by default, so a first run cannot remove a protection that predates the config.

$replace.description: In an override, replace the baseline's entries entirely instead of merging into them by key.
